related.note: China endorsed the Paris statement, which was also endorsed by India and Brazil but not by the United States or the United Kingdom.
China proposed the UNGA capacity-building resolution; the initiative likewise emphasises developing-country capacity.
The 2025 Global AI Governance Action Plan, a later Chinese document in the same policy line, refers to the Pact for the Future and the Global Digital Compact.

ai_provisions: Whole document — people-centred development, sovereignty, international law, military-AI prudence, risk-tiered testing, privacy, fairness, ethics and developing-country representation
Paragraph on military AI — all countries, especially major countries, should adopt a prudent and responsible attitude to military AI research, development and application
Paragraph on exclusivity — opposition to drawing ideological lines or forming exclusive groups and to technological monopolies and unilateral coercive measures
Final paragraph — support for UN-framework discussions on an international AI institution
relevance.excluded_scope: Unilateral policy initiative; no negotiating mandate, signature, ratification, endorsement procedure, monitoring or enforcement.
relevance.reason: A unilateral Chinese government proposal for international AI governance, announced by President Xi Jinping on 18 October 2023 and published in English by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It is not an agreed international instrument and creates no legal obligation, but it is a primary articulation of China's position on sovereignty, development, UN-centred governance, military-AI prudence and opposition to exclusive groups. It is included to document the Chinese pole of the international AI-governance debate alongside the U.S.-led military declaration and the Council of Europe treaty.
